overall: Committee violated the OML by deliberating via email on three occasions; prior release of minutes did not cure the Sept. 2020 email. Public comment and civility allegations declined; intent not found.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Vice Chair deliberated with a quorum of the committee via email on public business.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, we find that the Committee violated the Open Meeting Law by deliberating outside of a properly noticed meeting.

allegations.summary: Committee argued it cured the September 2020 email deliberation by releasing executive session minutes and the email with redactions.
allegations.key_passage: Although we commend the Committee for taking this remedial action, we find that this action was insufficient to fully remedy the violation.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Vice Chair conspired to prevent an individual from speaking at public comment.
allegations.key_passage: The Open Meeting Law does not require that a public body allow public participation in a meeting.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Vice Chair made negative comments about students and others.
allegations.key_passage: Likewise, although we certainly discourage uncivil and unprofessional behavior, an allegation of unprofessional conduct or incivility does not constitute a violation of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complainant urged that the email deliberation violation was intentional; the AG was asked to find intent under G.L. c. 30A, 23(c).
allegations.key_passage: We therefore decline to find that the violation was intentional.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law.
Release to the public the September 26, 2020, email in its entirety within 30 days of the date of the letter.
remedy_passage: Additionally, we order the Committee to release to the public the September 26, 2020, email in its entirety within 30 days of the date of this letter.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
